stages.name: Renewable and non-renewable resources
stages.title: Renewable and non-renewable resources
stages.sub: Why some scarce resources can be replaced and others cannot.

steps.q: Fish, timber and oil are scarce. Does that mean more can never be produced, or just that supply is limited right now?
steps.right: Just that there is a limited amount now
steps.wrong: That no more can ever be produced
steps.hint: Scarcity is about the amount available today, not about what happens over time.

steps.q: A forest is cut for timber, but new trees are planted and grow back. Managed well, can it keep supplying timber for ever?
steps.right: Yes, it can keep being replaced
steps.wrong: No, it will eventually run out
steps.hint: Think about what happens between one harvest and the next.

steps.q: An oil field is drilled dry and the oil burned. Can that same oil field ever supply oil again?
steps.right: No, it is gone for good
steps.hint: Oil takes millions of years to form. Does that happen again in time for us to use it?

steps.q: One country fuels itself from planted forests, another from coal mines. Fifty years on, whose supply is more likely to last?
steps.wrong: Both equally, since both are scarce
steps.hint: One can regrow, the other cannot be remade once dug up.
